title: Using AI as a vibecoding partner on a UE5 C++ gallic wars themed RTS
author: MorbilyABeast
selftext:
How I keep control of the outcome:

I write the design in Obsidian first: what a soldier senses, what triggers a break, how signifer buffs pass down.

I hand the AI a tight spec and ask for complete function replacements, not snippets.

I describe exactly what's wrong (for example, "the line breaks too early when the flank is still intact"), and iterate.

Anything that doesn't match the design gets thrown out. The AI speeds up implementation; the game design stays mine

comments.author: Much_Note_4951
comments.body: I have some questions, do you have experience in coding or game development? Or does the AI fully develop the game for you with your oversight of its outputs? I mean like also the models and mesh etc. From what I see so far, the graphics look good. The soldiers do move a bit erratically I won't lie but that is expected due to it still being early and developed on right? I like what you've done so far. What is obsidian by the way?

replies.author: MorbilyABeast
replies.body: Im not a coder but a 3d artist by profession. And familiar with some aspects of game dev. I just work on one system at a time with claude code. Iterating it slowly testing it reconciling,  rinse and repeat. Obsidian is just a note taking software. Organizes stuff in markdown format and claude writes down important information there for me to recall

replies.author: Much_Note_4951
replies.body: How do you do it? I am familiar with game development, still a beginner though. I understand some code, C++, python, etc. I've made small game implementations, did 3d model/mesh/asset work with blender. I just find game dev to be way too overwhelming now since I have work and cannot balance it. I don't even know where to start or begin or how would I even let AI code for me in UE.

replies.author: MorbilyABeast
replies.body: I just descrived it. I also do this stuff between my job. People over complicate it. Claude code 20 dollar plan. Opus 5.5. Medium for most, C++ as much as you can and avoid nodes. Work on a system at a time. Test it , continue. Thats it. I been doing that for a year and I dont even code. I guess I do have a good intuition for game design and what I like. But thats really it.

replies.author: Much_Note_4951
replies.body: Trust me haha I wish it was as easy as it sounds. How do you know which system to start out with? Which is the foundation? What to be working on next? What proper and good coding practices and testing should be used? How do systems interact with each other? etc etc. I was thinking claude $100 plan but idk I don't want to waste the money if the outputs are not up to standard. The game I am trying to make is a very deep simulation, hyper realistic medieval fantasy roguelike passion project (mostly for myself to enjoy). Think something like dwarf fortress adventure mode but way more complex. I wanted it to be 3rd person in unreal engine but it's like idk wtf I am doing haha.

replies.author: MorbilyABeast
replies.body: Just start. 20 dollar plan is all you need. Claude desktop. Point to porject files. C++. Ask him anything. Spitball ideas and write out a short gameplan. Them attack a core feature. I started with my soldiers spawning in a grid behind my player commander and following. Quite literally. And this was before claude code. I was copy pasting code bits from web browser into Visual studio lol . Compiling and testing. Writing back to him what I wanted next or didnt like. Rinse repeat. Checked ot off the list when I felt comfy and moved on. Over time stopped and focused on anywhere either could optimize. Then continued. Rinse repeat. Claude desktop made this 1000x easier than when I started. Not to mention its much much better than it was before. Knows unreal engine well. And almost never wrong when describing things I need to do to get a result in engine. Wasn't the case when i started a year ago. Just start. It will fall into place. Most important is if you are making progress and having fun. Seeing things work right in front of my eyes , putting my ideas in front of me and seeing them work and develop gives me boundless energy.

replies.author: Much_Note_4951
replies.body: How can you tell that the code follows good coding practices and isn't spaghetti or that the file structures are good and whatnot? I mean yeah I can go and hash out some systems and stuff but after a while of implementing stuff and systems that interact with each other, it gets stupid and it starts to break or reduce/change features etc. I tried to make all systems mostly modular so that they can be easily edited and don't fully rely on each other too much but it really eats up a lot of context.

replies.author: MorbilyABeast
replies.body: I dont concern myself with it. I try to make it modular as possible and design ahead best I can. But understand my limitations in code architecture knowlesgde and best peactices. Hasn't stopped me in over a year of developing. Is   a lot od it wasteful , confusing to read , or not very modular. Yes. But it works and everything is able to be iterated on so I continue. Its just a matter of the user. How much you are willing to allow just to be automated and how concerned youa re about engineering. Im mostly concerned about if it works. If its fun and if i can optimize or if it all all make something that can be reused.

replies.author: Much_Note_4951
replies.body: Makes sense. Was just afraid of the problem of future spaghetti code making it hard to implement and change things later on. Maybe I am overthinking it. You sure I shouldn't go with the $100 plan?

replies.author: MorbilyABeast
replies.body: Won't be hard if you have claude. Thats the beauty  of it. Idk do you man. 20 Ia enough for me. I find staying on thw computer too long isn't good. For your back. So the limits make me either go back to my real job making 3d or touch grass

comments.author: AlexanderGGA
comments.body: Would this have kingdom building like base building

replies.author: MorbilyABeast
replies.body: Think total war rome 2 gameplay loop with open world. There will be basebuilding and seigecraft. Also building bridges over rivers,  settlment upgrades, public order and terrain deformation which is currently in test phase
